+func (s *treeWriter) applyPreparedBatch(
+	ctx context.Context,
+	prepared *preparedBatchSessions,
+	existing *object.Tree,
+	basePath string,
+) (plumbing.Hash, batchBuildStats, error) {
+	var stats batchBuildStats
+	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
+		return plumbing.ZeroHash, stats, err //nolint:wrapcheck // Propagating context cancellation
+	}
+
+	rootEntries := make(map[string]object.TreeEntry)
+	if existing != nil {
+		for _, entry := range existing.Entries {
+			stats.RootEntriesVisited++
+			rootEntries[entry.Name] = entry
+		}
+	}
+
+	var existingSummary *CheckpointSummary
+	if entry, ok := rootEntries[paths.MetadataFileName]; ok {
+		var err error
+		existingSummary, err = s.readSummaryFromBlob(entry.Hash)
+		if err != nil {
+			return plumbing.ZeroHash, stats, fmt.Errorf("read existing checkpoint summary: %w", err)
+		}
+		if existingSummary.CheckpointID != prepared.request.CheckpointID {
+			return plumbing.ZeroHash, stats, fmt.Errorf("existing checkpoint summary ID %s does not match batch checkpoint ID %s", existingSummary.CheckpointID, prepared.request.CheckpointID)
+		}
+	} else if existing != nil && len(existing.Entries) != 0 {
+		return plumbing.ZeroHash, stats, errors.New("existing checkpoint tree has no root metadata")
+	}
+
+	var sessionPaths []SessionFilePaths
+	finalByID := make(map[string]finalBatchSession)
+	indexBySession := make(map[string]int)
+	if existingSummary != nil {
+		sessionPaths = append([]SessionFilePaths(nil), existingSummary.Sessions...)
+		for index := range existingSummary.Sessions {
+			entry, ok := rootEntries[strconv.Itoa(index)]
+			if !ok || entry.Mode != filemode.Dir {
+				return plumbing.ZeroHash, stats, fmt.Errorf("existing session %d subtree is missing", index)
+			}
+			metadata, err := s.readSessionMetadataFromSubtree(entry.Hash, &stats)
+			if err != nil {
+				return plumbing.ZeroHash, stats, fmt.Errorf("read existing session %d metadata: %w", index, err)
+			}
+			if _, duplicate := finalByID[metadata.SessionID]; duplicate {
+				return plumbing.ZeroHash, stats, fmt.Errorf("existing checkpoint repeats session ID %q", metadata.SessionID)
+			}
+			finalByID[metadata.SessionID] = finalSessionFromMetadata(metadata)
+			indexBySession[metadata.SessionID] = index
+		}
+	}
+
+	nextSessionIndex := len(sessionPaths)
+	for _, incoming := range prepared.sessions {
+		index, exists := indexBySession[incoming.opts.SessionID]
+		if !exists {
+			index = nextSessionIndex
+			nextSessionIndex++
+			indexBySession[incoming.opts.SessionID] = index
+			sessionPaths = append(sessionPaths, SessionFilePaths{})
+		}
+		rootEntries[strconv.Itoa(index)] = object.TreeEntry{
+			Name: strconv.Itoa(index), Mode: filemode.Dir, Hash: incoming.treeHash,
+		}
+		sessionPaths[index] = qualifySessionFilePaths(basePath, index, incoming.filePaths)
+		finalByID[incoming.opts.SessionID] = finalBatchSession{
+			metadata:  incoming.metadata,
+			hasReview: incoming.opts.HasReview || incoming.metadata.Kind == checkpointKindAgentReview,
+			hasInvestigation: incoming.opts.HasInvestigation ||
+				incoming.metadata.Kind == checkpointKindAgentInvestigate,
+			imported: incoming.opts.Kind == checkpointKindImported,
+		}
+	}
+
+	if len(prepared.tasks) > 0 {
+		tasksHash, err := s.mergePreparedTasks(rootEntries, prepared.tasks, &stats)
+		if err != nil {
+			return plumbing.ZeroHash, stats, err
+		}
+		rootEntries["tasks"] = object.TreeEntry{Name: "tasks", Mode: filemode.Dir, Hash: tasksHash}
+	}
+
+	summary := reduceBatchSummary(prepared.request.CheckpointID, existingSummary, sessionPaths, finalByID, &stats)
+	metadataJSON, err := jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline(summary, "", "  ")
+	if err != nil {
+		return plumbing.ZeroHash, stats, fmt.Errorf("marshal checkpoint summary: %w", err)
+	}
+	metadataHash, err := CreateBlobFromContent(s.repo, metadataJSON)
+	if err != nil {
+		return plumbing.ZeroHash, stats, fmt.Errorf("create checkpoint summary blob: %w", err)
+	}
+	rootEntries[paths.MetadataFileName] = object.TreeEntry{
+		Name: paths.MetadataFileName, Mode: filemode.Regular, Hash: metadataHash,
+	}
+
+	rootHash, err := storeTreeEntryMap(s.repo, rootEntries)
+	if err != nil {
+		return plumbing.ZeroHash, stats, fmt.Errorf("store checkpoint root tree: %w", err)
+	}
+	return rootHash, stats, nil
+}
+
+func (s *treeWriter) readSessionMetadataFromSubtree(hash plumbing.Hash, stats *batchBuildStats) (*Metadata, error) {
+	tree, err := s.repo.TreeObject(hash)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("read session subtree: %w", err)
+	}
+	for _, entry := range tree.Entries {
+		stats.SessionEntriesVisited++
+		if entry.Name == paths.MetadataFileName && entry.Mode != filemode.Dir {
+			stats.ExistingMetadataRead++
+			return s.readMetadataFromBlob(entry.Hash)
+		}
+	}
+	return nil, errors.New("metadata.json not found")
+}
+
+func (s *treeWriter) mergePreparedTasks(
+	rootEntries map[string]object.TreeEntry,
+	prepared map[string]plumbing.Hash,
+	stats *batchBuildStats,
+) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
+	taskEntries := make(map[string]object.TreeEntry)
+	if existing, ok := rootEntries["tasks"]; ok {
+		if existing.Mode != filemode.Dir {
+			return plumbing.ZeroHash, errors.New("existing tasks entry is not a directory")
+		}
+		tree, err := s.repo.TreeObject(existing.Hash)
+		if err != nil {
+			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("read existing tasks tree: %w", err)
+		}
+		for _, entry := range tree.Entries {
+			stats.TaskEntriesVisited++
+			taskEntries[entry.Name] = entry
+		}
+	}
+	for toolUseID, hash := range prepared {
+		taskEntries[toolUseID] = object.TreeEntry{Name: toolUseID, Mode: filemode.Dir, Hash: hash}
+	}
+	return storeTreeEntryMap(s.repo, taskEntries)
+}
+
+func reduceBatchSummary(
+	checkpointID id.CheckpointID,
+	existing *CheckpointSummary,
+	sessionPaths []SessionFilePaths,
+	finalByID map[string]finalBatchSession,
+	stats *batchBuildStats,
+) *CheckpointSummary {
+	orderedIDs := make([]string, 0, len(finalByID))
+	for sessionID := range finalByID {
+		orderedIDs = append(orderedIDs, sessionID)
+	}
+	sort.Strings(orderedIDs)
+
+	summary := &CheckpointSummary{
+		CheckpointID: checkpointID,
+		CLIVersion:   versioninfo.Version,
+		Sessions:     sessionPaths,
+	}
+	if existing != nil {
+		summary.CommitSHA = existing.CommitSHA
+		summary.CombinedAttribution = existing.CombinedAttribution
+		summary.HasReview = existing.HasReview
+		summary.HasInvestigation = existing.HasInvestigation
+		summary.Imported = existing.Imported
+	}
+	files := make(map[string]struct{})
+	for _, sessionID := range orderedIDs {
+		stats.FinalSessionContributions++
+		final := finalByID[sessionID]
+		metadata := final.metadata
+		summary.Strategy = metadata.Strategy
+		summary.Branch = metadata.Branch
+		if metadata.CommitSHA != "" {
+			summary.CommitSHA = metadata.CommitSHA
+		}
+		summary.CheckpointsCount += metadata.CheckpointsCount
+		summary.TokenUsage = types.AddTokenUsage(summary.TokenUsage, metadata.TokenUsage)
+		summary.HasReview = summary.HasReview || final.hasReview
+		summary.HasInvestigation = summary.HasInvestigation || final.hasInvestigation
+		summary.Imported = summary.Imported || final.imported
+		for _, file := range metadata.FilesTouched {
+			files[filepath.ToSlash(file)] = struct{}{}
+		}
+	}
+	if len(files) > 0 {
+		summary.FilesTouched = make([]string, 0, len(files))
+		for file := range files {
+			summary.FilesTouched = append(summary.FilesTouched, file)
+		}
+		sort.Strings(summary.FilesTouched)
+	}
+	return summary
+}
+
+func finalSessionFromMetadata(metadata *Metadata) finalBatchSession {
+	return finalBatchSession{
+		metadata:         metadata,
+		hasReview:        metadata.Kind == checkpointKindAgentReview,
+		hasInvestigation: metadata.Kind == checkpointKindAgentInvestigate,
+		imported:         metadata.Kind == checkpointKindImported,
+	}
+}
+
+func qualifySessionFilePaths(basePath string, index int, relative SessionFilePaths) SessionFilePaths {
+	qualify := func(value string) string {
+		if value == "" {
+			return ""
+		}
+		return "/" + checkpointSubtreePath(basePath, strconv.Itoa(index), strings.TrimPrefix(value, "/"))
+	}
+	return SessionFilePaths{
+		Metadata:          qualify(relative.Metadata),
+		Transcript:        qualify(relative.Transcript),
+		CompactTranscript: qualify(relative.CompactTranscript),
+		ContentHash:       qualify(relative.ContentHash),
+		Prompt:            qualify(relative.Prompt),
+		AssetsManifest:    qualify(relative.AssetsManifest),
+	}
+}
+
+func storeTreeEntryMap(repo *git.Repository, entries map[string]object.TreeEntry) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
+	ordered := make([]object.TreeEntry, 0, len(entries))
+	for name, entry := range entries {
+		entry.Name = name
+		ordered = append(ordered, entry)
+	}
+	sortTreeEntries(ordered)
+	return storeTree(repo, ordered)
+}
+
+func buildBatchCommitMessage(req BatchSessions) string {
+	var message strings.Builder
+	fmt.Fprintf(&message, "Checkpoint: %s\n\n", req.CheckpointID)
+	if req.CommitSubject != "" {
+		message.WriteString(req.CommitSubject)
+		message.WriteString("\n\n")
+	}
+	for _, session := range req.Sessions {
+		fmt.Fprintf(&message, "%s: %s\n", trailers.SessionTrailerKey, WriteOptions(session).SessionID)
+	}
+	if value, common := commonBatchValue(req.Sessions, func(opts WriteOptions) string { return opts.Strategy }); common {
+		fmt.Fprintf(&message, "%s: %s\n", trailers.StrategyTrailerKey, value)
+	}
+	if value, common := commonBatchValue(req.Sessions, func(opts WriteOptions) string { return string(opts.Agent) }); common && value != "" {
+		fmt.Fprintf(&message, "%s: %s\n", trailers.AgentTrailerKey, value)
+	}
+	if value, common := commonBatchValue(req.Sessions, func(opts WriteOptions) string { return opts.EphemeralBranch }); common && value != "" {
+		fmt.Fprintf(&message, "%s: %s\n", trailers.EphemeralBranchTrailerKey, value)
+	}
+	return message.String()
+}
+
+func commonBatchValue(sessions []ReservedSession, value func(WriteOptions) string) (string, bool) {
+	first := value(WriteOptions(sessions[0]))
+	for _, session := range sessions[1:] {
+		if value(WriteOptions(session)) != first {

 // Individual branch deletion failures do not stop the operation - all branches are attempted.

 func hasReachableShallowBoundary(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, repoPath string, hashes ...string) (bool, error) {
 	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)
 	defer cancel()
 
 	shallowHashes, err := repo.Storer.Shallow()
 	if err != nil {
 		return false, fmt.Errorf("read shallow commits: %w", err)
 	}
 	if len(shallowHashes) == 0 {
 		return false, nil
 	}
 
 	shallowCommits := make(map[string]struct{}, len(shallowHashes))
 	for _, hash := range shallowHashes {
 		shallowCommits[hash.String()] = struct{}{}
 	}
 	for _, hash := range hashes {
 		reachesBoundary, err := historyReachesShallowBoundary(ctx, repoPath, hash, shallowCommits)
 		if err != nil {
 			return false, err
 		}
 		if reachesBoundary {
 			return true, nil
 		}
 	}
 	return false, nil
 }
 
 func historyReachesShallowBoundary(ctx context.Context, repoPath, hash string, shallowCommits map[string]struct{}) (bool, error) {
 	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-list", hash)
 	cmd.Dir = repoPath
 	output, err := cmd.Output()
 	if err != nil {
 		return false, fmt.Errorf("git rev-list %s failed: %w", hash, err)
 	}
 	for _, commitHash := range strings.Fields(string(output)) {
 		if _, ok := shallowCommits[commitHash]; ok {
 			return true, nil
 		}
 	}
 	return false, nil
 }

 func checkpointInfosFromCommitted(committed []checkpoint.CheckpointInfo) []CheckpointInfo {
 	result := make([]CheckpointInfo, 0, len(committed))
 	for _, c := range committed {
 		result = append(result, CheckpointInfo{
 			CheckpointID:     c.CheckpointID,
 			SessionID:        c.SessionID,
 			CreatedAt:        c.CreatedAt,
 			CheckpointsCount: c.CheckpointsCount,
 			FilesTouched:     c.FilesTouched,
 			Agent:            c.Agent,
 			IsTask:           c.IsTask,
 			ToolUseID:        c.ToolUseID,
 			SessionCount:     c.SessionCount,
 			SessionIDs:       c.SessionIDs,
 			Imported:         c.Imported,
 		})
 	}
 	sort.Slice(result, func(i, j int) bool {
 		return result[i].CreatedAt.After(result[j].CreatedAt)

 // ExtractFirstPrompt extracts and truncates the first meaningful prompt from prompt content.
 // Prompts are separated by "\n\n---\n\n". Skips empty prompts and separator-only content.
 // Returns empty string if no valid prompt is found.
 func ExtractFirstPrompt(content string) string {
 	if content == "" {
 		return ""
 	}
 
 	// Prompts are separated by "\n\n---\n\n"
 	// Find the first non-empty prompt
 	prompts := strings.Split(content, "\n\n---\n\n")
 	var firstPrompt string
 	for _, p := range prompts {
 		cleaned := strings.TrimSpace(p)
 		// Skip empty prompts or prompts that are just dashes/separators
 		if cleaned == "" || isOnlySeparators(cleaned) {
 			continue
 		}
 		firstPrompt = cleaned
 		break
 	}

 // ensureSessionInitialized creates the session state file if it doesn't yet
 // exist (or has empty BaseCommit). Idempotent: the existence check and the
 // create both happen inside initializeSession's session gate so a concurrent
 // turn-start hook can't slip a richer state in between, only to have it
 // overwritten with blank fields.
 func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) ensureSessionInitialized(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, sessionID string, agentTypeHint types.AgentType) error {
 	state, err := s.loadSessionState(ctx, sessionID)
 	if err != nil {
 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to load session state: %w", err)
 	}
 	agentType := resolveAgentType(agentTypeHint, state)
 	if err := s.initializeSession(ctx, repo, sessionID, agentType, "", "", ""); err != nil {
 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to initialize session: %w", err)
 	}
 	return nil
 }

 // mergeFilesTouched merges multiple file lists into existing touched files, deduplicating.
 // All paths are normalized to forward slashes for platform-agnostic storage.
 func mergeFilesTouched(existing []string, fileLists ...[]string) []string {
 	seen := make(map[string]bool)
 	for _, f := range existing {
 		seen[filepath.ToSlash(f)] = true
 	}
 
 	for _, list := range fileLists {
 		for _, f := range list {
 			seen[filepath.ToSlash(f)] = true
 		}
 	}
 
 	result := make([]string, 0, len(seen))
 	for f := range seen {
 		result = append(result, f)
 	}
 
 	// Sort for deterministic output
 	sort.Strings(result)
 	return result
 }

 // WarnIfMetadataDisconnected checks (once per process) whether the metadata
 // branch is disconnected and prints a warning to stderr if so. The check runs
 // against the first checkpoint read candidate whose remote-tracking ref
 // exists (pure read across both tiers).
 // It does NOT fix the problem — users are directed to 'entire doctor'.
 //
 // Takes the caller's context rather than context.Background(): the probe below
 // reads git, so a detached context ignored both interrupt cancellation and the
 // invocation-scoped remote-read cache, re-shelling out for answers the caller
 // already had.
 //
 // Uses sync.Once, so a transient failure on the first call permanently suppresses
 // the warning. This is acceptable because the check is advisory only and
 // 'entire doctor' is the authoritative repair path.
 func WarnIfMetadataDisconnected(ctx context.Context) {
 	disconnectedOnce.Do(func() {
 		repo, err := OpenRepository(ctx)
 		if err != nil {
 			logging.Debug(ctx, "metadata disconnection check: could not open repository",
 				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
 			return
 		}
 		defer repo.Close()
 		refs := checkpoint.ResolveRefs(ctx)
 		if !refs.PrimaryFetchableFromRemote() {
 			return // no remote tracks Primary; nothing to disconnect from
 		}
 		_, remoteRefName, ok := FirstReadCandidateTrackingRef(ctx, repo, refs.Primary)
 		if !ok {
 			return // no candidate has a tracking ref; nothing to disconnect from
 		}
 		disconnected, err := IsMetadataDisconnected(ctx, repo, remoteRefName)
 		if err != nil {
 			logging.Debug(ctx, "metadata disconnection check failed",
 				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
 			return
 		}
 		if !disconnected {
 			return
 		}
 		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "[entire] Warning: Local and remote session metadata branches are disconnected.")
 		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "[entire] Some checkpoints from remote may not be visible. Run 'entire doctor' to fix.")
 	})
 }

 // isDisconnected checks if two commits have no common ancestor using git merge-base.
 // Returns (true, nil) if disconnected, (false, nil) if they share ancestry,
 // or (false, error) if git merge-base failed for another reason.
 //
 // git merge-base exit codes:
 //   - 0: common ancestor found (shared ancestry)
 //   - 1: no common ancestor (disconnected)
 //   - 128+: error (corrupt repo, invalid hash, etc.)
 func isDisconnected(ctx context.Context, repoPath, hashA, hashB string) (bool, error) {
 	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)
 	defer cancel()
 	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "merge-base", hashA, hashB)
 	cmd.Dir = repoPath
 	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
 		var exitErr *exec.ExitError
 		if errors.As(err, &exitErr) && exitErr.ExitCode() == 1 {
 			return true, nil // No common ancestor — disconnected
 		}
 		return false, fmt.Errorf("git merge-base failed: %w", err)
 	}
 	return false, nil // Shared ancestry
 }
 
 // collectCommitChain walks from tip to root following first parent, returns oldest-first.
 // Commits listed in shallow are treated as roots — the walk stops at them without
 // traversing into their parents. go-git's repo.CommitObject().ParentHashes does not
 // consult .git/shallow on its own, so without this check the walk would stroll past
 // shallow boundaries into stale objects left in the pack (e.g., when the remote
 // branch has been rebuilt since the last full fetch), producing a phantom chain of
 // commits that no longer represent the actual checkpoint history.
 func collectCommitChain(repo *git.Repository, tip plumbing.Hash, shallow map[plumbing.Hash]bool) ([]*object.Commit, error) {
 	var chain []*object.Commit
 	current := tip
 
 	reachedRoot := false
 	for range MaxCommitTraversalDepth {
 		commit, err := repo.CommitObject(current)
 		if err != nil {
 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit %s: %w", current, err)
 		}
 		chain = append(chain, commit)
 
 		if len(commit.ParentHashes) == 0 {
 			reachedRoot = true
 			break
 		}
 		if shallow[current] {
 			// Shallow boundary — treat as a root.
 			reachedRoot = true
 			break
 		}
 		current = commit.ParentHashes[0]
 	}
 
 	if !reachedRoot {
 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("commit chain exceeded %d commits without reaching root; aborting reconciliation", MaxCommitTraversalDepth)
 	}
 
 	// Reverse to oldest-first
 	for i, j := 0, len(chain)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
 		chain[i], chain[j] = chain[j], chain[i]
 	}
 
 	return chain, nil
 }
 
 // loadShallowHashes returns the commit hashes listed in the repository's
 // shallow file, or an empty map if the repository is not shallow.
 func loadShallowHashes(ctx context.Context, repoPath string) (map[plumbing.Hash]bool, error) {
 	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir")
 	cmd.Dir = repoPath
 	out, err := cmd.Output()
 	if err != nil {
 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("git rev-parse --git-common-dir: %w", err)
 	}
 	gitDir := strings.TrimSpace(string(out))

 // mergeFilesTouched merges multiple file lists into existing touched files, deduplicating.
 // All paths are normalized to forward slashes for platform-agnostic storage.
 func mergeFilesTouched(existing []string, fileLists ...[]string) []string {
 	seen := make(map[string]bool)
 	for _, f := range existing {
 		seen[filepath.ToSlash(f)] = true
 	}
 
 	for _, list := range fileLists {
 		for _, f := range list {
 			seen[filepath.ToSlash(f)] = true
 		}
 	}
 
 	result := make([]string, 0, len(seen))
 	for f := range seen {
 		result = append(result, f)
 	}
 
 	// Sort for deterministic output
 	sort.Strings(result)
 	return result
 }

 // isDisconnected checks if two commits have no common ancestor using git merge-base.
 // Returns (true, nil) if disconnected, (false, nil) if they share ancestry,
 // or (false, error) if git merge-base failed for another reason.
 //
 // git merge-base exit codes:
 //   - 0: common ancestor found (shared ancestry)
 //   - 1: no common ancestor (disconnected)
 //   - 128+: error (corrupt repo, invalid hash, etc.)
 func isDisconnected(ctx context.Context, repoPath, hashA, hashB string) (bool, error) {
 	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)
 	defer cancel()
 	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "merge-base", hashA, hashB)
 	cmd.Dir = repoPath
 	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
 		var exitErr *exec.ExitError
 		if errors.As(err, &exitErr) && exitErr.ExitCode() == 1 {
 			return true, nil // No common ancestor — disconnected
 		}
 		return false, fmt.Errorf("git merge-base failed: %w", err)
 	}
 	return false, nil // Shared ancestry
 }
 
 // collectCommitChain walks from tip to root following first parent, returns oldest-first.
 // Commits listed in shallow are treated as roots — the walk stops at them without
 // traversing into their parents. go-git's repo.CommitObject().ParentHashes does not
 // consult .git/shallow on its own, so without this check the walk would stroll past
 // shallow boundaries into stale objects left in the pack (e.g., when the remote
 // branch has been rebuilt since the last full fetch), producing a phantom chain of
 // commits that no longer represent the actual checkpoint history.
 func collectCommitChain(repo *git.Repository, tip plumbing.Hash, shallow map[plumbing.Hash]bool) ([]*object.Commit, error) {
 	var chain []*object.Commit
 	current := tip
 
 	reachedRoot := false
 	for range MaxCommitTraversalDepth {
 		commit, err := repo.CommitObject(current)
 		if err != nil {
 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit %s: %w", current, err)
 		}
 		chain = append(chain, commit)
 
 		if len(commit.ParentHashes) == 0 {
 			reachedRoot = true
 			break
 		}
 		if shallow[current] {
 			// Shallow boundary — treat as a root.
 			reachedRoot = true
 			break
 		}
 		current = commit.ParentHashes[0]
 	}
 
 	if !reachedRoot {
 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("commit chain exceeded %d commits without reaching root; aborting reconciliation", MaxCommitTraversalDepth)
 	}
 
 	// Reverse to oldest-first
 	for i, j := 0, len(chain)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
 		chain[i], chain[j] = chain[j], chain[i]
 	}
 
 	return chain, nil
 }

    56		}

    58		committed, err := store.List(ctx)
    59		if err != nil {
    60			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to list committed checkpoints: %w", err)
    61		}
    62	
    63		return checkpointInfosFromCommitted(committed), nil
    64	}

    81		if err != nil {

   101		headTree         *object.Tree        // Pre-resolved HEAD tree (passed through to calculateSessionAttributions)
   102		parentTree       *object.Tree        // Pre-resolved parent tree (nil for initial commits, for consistent non-agent line counting)
   103		repoDir          string              // Repository worktree path for git CLI commands
   104		parentCommitHash string              // HEAD's first parent hash for per-commit non-agent file detection
   105		headCommitHash   string              // HEAD commit hash (passed through for attribution)

   109		// checkpoint ID than the caller passed, when it recognises the transcript
   110		// range in a checkpoint left behind by an interrupted write from a CLI that
   111		// predates reservations. Only a caller that chooses the ID itself may set it.
   112		//
   113		// PostCommit must NOT: its ID comes from the commit's Entire-Checkpoint
   114		// trailer, which is already written and cannot be revised. Redirecting the
   115		// write there leaves the commit naming a checkpoint that was never stored,
   116		// and updateCombinedAttributionForCheckpoint writing attribution under the

   132	// eight always-on/opt-in layers) over a session transcript at
   133	// post-commit condensation. OPF is intentionally NOT included here —
   134	// it runs exclusively in the pre-push rewrite path
   135	// (strategy/manual_commit_opf_rewrite.go), which re-redacts the

   137	// the push.
   138	//
   139	// Exposed as a var so tests can inject deterministic success/error
   140	// returns. The signature still takes a context so the var can be

   146	// extractSessionImages lifts inline base64 images out of a transcript into
   147	// externalized assets via the per-agent image codec, returning the rewritten
   148	// (placeholder-bearing) transcript. Agents with no codec, or transcripts with no
   149	// externalizable images, pass through unchanged. Injectable for tests.
   150	var extractSessionImages = func(agentType types.AgentType, transcript []byte) ([]byte, []cpkg.TranscriptAsset, error) {
   151		codec := imageextract.CodecFor(agentType)
   152		if codec == nil {
   153			return transcript, nil, nil
   154		}
   155		rewritten, assets, err := codec.ExtractImages(transcript)
   156		if err != nil {
   157			return transcript, nil, fmt.Errorf("extract images: %w", err)
   158		}
   159		if len(assets) == 0 {
   160			return transcript, nil, nil
   161		}
   162		out := make([]cpkg.TranscriptAsset, len(assets))
   163		for i, a := range assets {
   164			out[i] = cpkg.TranscriptAsset{Name: a.Name, MediaType: a.MediaType, Data: a.Data}
   165		}
   166		return rewritten, out, nil
   167	}

   169	// externalizeSessionImages runs the opt-in image-externalization step over a
   170	// session transcript before redaction. When enabled it returns the rewritten
   171	// (placeholder-bearing) transcript plus the extracted assets; when disabled,
   172	// unsupported for the agent, or on error it returns the transcript unchanged with
   173	// nil assets (the checkpoint then stores the inline transcript).
   174	//
   175	// It deliberately does NOT mutate the caller's transcript: the pre-externalization
   176	// bytes are what CondenseResult.TranscriptSizeBaseline is measured on, and that
   177	// baseline must stay in the shadow-branch blob's coordinate (sanitized but NOT
   178	// image-externalized, matching what the Stop path writes) — feeding it the shrunken
   179	// externalized size would report spurious growth on every subsequent commit.
   180	func externalizeSessionImages(ctx, logCtx context.Context, state *SessionState, transcript []byte) ([]byte, []cpkg.TranscriptAsset) {
   181		if !settings.IsImageExternalizationEnabled(ctx) {
   182			return transcript, nil
   183		}
   184		rewritten, assets, err := extractSessionImages(state.AgentType, transcript)
   185		if err != nil {
   186			logging.Warn(logCtx, "image externalization failed; leaving transcript inline",
   187				slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   188				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   189			return transcript, nil
   190		}
   191		return rewritten, assets
   192	}

   194	// prepareTranscriptForStorage runs the first two steps of the stored-copy pipeline
   195	// in order — sanitize (drop non-portable agent state), then externalize inline
   196	// images. Redaction is the caller's next step, so the whole pipeline reads
   197	// sanitize -> externalize -> redact. See prepareTaskTranscriptForStorage for
   198	// the twin that runs the same pipeline over a subagent's own transcript.
   199	//
   200	// Each step has to precede the next:
   201	//
   202	//   - Sanitize first, so we neither externalize images out of items we are about to
   203	//     discard — which would store an asset whose referencing transcript line is gone
   204	//     moments later — nor redact megabytes of ciphertext only to throw it away.
   205	//     Base64 is the pathological input for the entropy layer, so on a large Codex
   206	//     rollout that scan alone costs tens of seconds.
   207	//   - Externalize before redaction, because base64 is high-entropy and redaction
   208	//     would otherwise flag and destroy it.
   209	//
   210	// It returns the sanitized size rather than the sanitized bytes: that size is the
   211	// coordinate the CheckpointTranscriptSize growth baseline must use (see
   212	// CondenseResult.TranscriptSizeBaseline), and returning the slice would keep a
   213	// second multi-MB buffer reachable for the rest of the condensation just to read
   214	// its length.
   215	func prepareTranscriptForStorage(
   216		ctx, logCtx context.Context,
   217		ag agent.Agent,
   218		state *SessionState,
   219		raw []byte,
   220	) (externalized []byte, assets []cpkg.TranscriptAsset, sanitizedSize int64) {
   221		sanitized := agent.SanitizeTranscriptForStorage(ag, raw)
   222		externalized, assets = externalizeSessionImages(ctx, logCtx, state, sanitized)
   223		return externalized, assets, int64(len(sanitized))
   224	}
   225	
   226	// prepareTaskTranscriptForStorage runs the sanitize -> externalize -> redact
   227	// chain for a single subagent transcript, mirroring prepareTranscriptForStorage's
   228	// first two steps and then completing with the same redaction the session
   229	// transcript gets (see redactSessionTranscript). It is a SEPARATE entry point
   230	// rather than a wrapper around prepareTranscriptForStorage for one reason:
   231	// that function returns the session transcript's sanitized SIZE, which seeds
   232	// CondenseResult.TranscriptSizeBaseline — the session's own growth-dedup
   233	// baseline (SessionState.CheckpointTranscriptSize). A task transcript must
   234	// NEVER contribute to that coordinate (it is not the session transcript), so
   235	// this helper only returns the pipeline's terminal artifacts: redacted bytes
   236	// and any externalized image assets. Callers append the assets to the
   237	// checkpoint's own Assets list (TaskPayload has no Assets field of its own).
   238	//
   239	// It also carries checkpoint.prepareSubagentTranscript's size guard, for the
   240	// same reason: agent-<agent-id>.jsonl is neither chunked nor capped, and
   240	// same reason: agent-<agent-id>.jsonl is neither chunked nor capped, and
   241	// redaction runs at roughly 220ms/MB. The cap is measured against the SANITIZED
   242	// bytes, not the raw ones — sanitizing strips the bulk (Codex encrypted_content
   243	// runs to ~20% of a rollout's bytes), so measuring raw would drop a transcript
   244	// oversized only by payloads about to be discarded.
   245	func prepareTaskTranscriptForStorage(
   246		ctx, logCtx context.Context,
   247		ag agent.Agent,
   248		state *SessionState,
   249		path string,
   250		raw []byte,
   251	) (redacted redact.RedactedBytes, assets []cpkg.TranscriptAsset, tooLarge bool, err error) {
   252		sanitized := agent.SanitizeTranscriptForStorage(ag, raw)
   253		if len(sanitized) > agent.MaxChunkSize {
   254			logging.Warn(logCtx, "subagent transcript exceeds the blob size cap; storing task without it",
   255				slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   256				slog.String("path", path),
   257				slog.Int("raw_bytes", len(raw)),
   258				slog.Int("sanitized_bytes", len(sanitized)),
   259				slog.Int("cap", agent.MaxChunkSize))
   260			return redact.RedactedBytes{}, nil, true, nil
   261		}
   262		externalized, assets := externalizeSessionImages(ctx, logCtx, state, sanitized)
   263		// nil repo declines prefix reuse: a subagent transcript is written once per
   264		// task, not appended across checkpoints, so there is nothing to reuse.
   265		redacted, _, err = redactSessionTranscript(logCtx, nil, "", externalized)
   266		if err != nil {
   267			return redact.RedactedBytes{}, nil, false, err
   268		}
   269		return redacted, assets, false, nil
   270	}

   272	// resolveTaskTranscriptPath falls back to the agent-layout convention when a
   273	// task record has no declared transcript path (e.g. an agent that reports the
   274	// path only on some events, or a legacy record captured before an agent
   275	// started reporting one at all). Mirrors cli.ResolveAgentTranscriptPath,
   276	// which this package cannot call directly — the cli package imports strategy,
   277	// so the reverse import would cycle — and the logic itself is small enough
   278	// that duplicating it here beats introducing a new shared package for this
   279	// one call site (moving the transcript resolver into paths is deliberately
   280	// out of scope for the durable-records plan this implements).
   281	func resolveTaskTranscriptPath(state *SessionState, agentID string) string {
   282		if agentID == "" || state.TranscriptPath == "" {
   283			return ""
   284		}
   285		transcriptDir := filepath.Dir(state.TranscriptPath)
   286		name := paths.AgentTranscriptFileName(agentID)
   287		if nested := filepath.Join(paths.SubagentsDir(transcriptDir, state.SessionID), name); fileExists(nested) {
   288			return nested
   289		}
   290		if legacy := filepath.Join(transcriptDir, name); fileExists(legacy) {
   291			return legacy
   292		}
   293		return ""
   294	}
   295	
   296	// taskTranscriptReasonUnresolvable, taskTranscriptReasonUnreadable,
   297	// taskTranscriptReasonEmpty, taskTranscriptReasonRedactionFailed, and
   298	// taskTranscriptReasonTooLarge are the stable
   299	// TaskPayload.TranscriptUnavailableReason categories. They deliberately
   300	// carry no path or underlying-error detail: task.json is pushed to
   301	// entire/checkpoints/v1, so a local filesystem path (which os.ReadFile's error
   302	// text embeds) must never end up in it. The detailed error goes only to
   303	// logging.Warn at the call site.
   304	const (
   305		taskTranscriptReasonUnresolvable    = "transcript path unresolvable"
   306		taskTranscriptReasonUnreadable      = "transcript unreadable"
   307		taskTranscriptReasonEmpty           = "transcript empty"
   308		taskTranscriptReasonRedactionFailed = "transcript redaction failed"
   309		taskTranscriptReasonTooLarge        = "transcript too large"
   310	)
   311	
   312	// materializeTaskRecords resolves and redacts each of state.TaskRecords'
   313	// subagent transcripts for storage under this checkpoint's
   314	// tasks/<tool-use-id>/ subtree — the durable-records materializer for #2058:
   315	// subagent transcripts used to die at condensation because no producer ever
   316	// set the (now deleted) WriteOptions.IsTask route.
   317	//
   318	// Every record is materialized on every condensation, whether completed or
   319	// still in flight: a completed record's transcript is stored once here and
   320	// then removed from session state by the caller (see resetCheckpointWindow);
   321	// an in-flight record's transcript-so-far is stored and the record stays so
   322	// the next condensation re-materializes it. A record whose transcript cannot
   323	// be resolved or read still produces a payload — with TranscriptUnavailableReason
   324	// set instead of a Transcript — so the pointer is never silently dropped.
   325	//
   326	// A record with an unsafe or empty ToolUseID, or one whose AgentID is unsafe
   327	// or empty at the point a transcript would be written, is skipped entirely —
   328	// no payload at all, not even a reason-only one: an unsafe ToolUseID has no
   329	// safe tasks/<id>/ directory to put a task.json under in the first place, and
   330	// an empty/unsafe AgentID would corrupt the agent-<id>.jsonl filename (see
   331	// writeTaskRecordEntries, which re-validates as a last resort). This must
   332	// never wedge condensation — a poisoned record produces zero payloads, not an
   333	// error, and the caller's normal completed-record removal
   334	// (resetCheckpointWindow) still drops it once completed, since a record that
   335	// can never materialize would otherwise retry forever.
   336	//
   337	// Task assets are appended to the incoming assets slice and returned (rather
   338	// than living on TaskPayload, which has no Assets field of its own) so they
   339	// join the checkpoint's own Assets list — see WriteOptions.Assets.
   340	func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) materializeTaskRecords(
   341		ctx, logCtx context.Context,
   342		ag agent.Agent,
   343		state *SessionState,
   344		assets []cpkg.TranscriptAsset,
   345	) ([]cpkg.TaskPayload, []cpkg.TranscriptAsset) {
   346		if len(state.TaskRecords) == 0 {
   347			return nil, assets
   348		}
   349	
   350		payloads := make([]cpkg.TaskPayload, 0, len(state.TaskRecords))
   351		for _, record := range state.TaskRecords {
   352			if record.ToolUseID == "" || validation.ValidateToolUseID(record.ToolUseID) != nil {
   353				logging.Warn(logCtx, "skipping task record: unsafe or empty tool_use_id",
   354					slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   355					slog.String("tool_use_id", record.ToolUseID),
   356				)
   357				continue
   358			}
   359	
   360			payload := cpkg.TaskPayload{
   361				ToolUseID:       record.ToolUseID,
   362				AgentID:         record.AgentID,
   363				SubagentType:    record.SubagentType,
   364				TaskDescription: record.TaskDescription,
   365				Files:           record.Files,
   366				TokenUsage:      record.TokenUsage,
   367				StartedAt:       record.StartedAt,
   368				CompletedAt:     record.CompletedAt,
   369			}
   370	
   371			// Candidate transcript paths, tried in order: the agent-declared path
   372			// first, then the agent-layout fallback — declared paths are
   373			// unreliable (agents relocate/clean up transcripts), which is why the
   374			// fallback resolver exists at all, so a declared-but-unreadable path
   375			// must not short-circuit past it.
   376			var candidates []string
   377			if record.DeclaredTranscriptPath != "" {
   378				candidates = append(candidates, record.DeclaredTranscriptPath)
   379			}
   380			if fallback := resolveTaskTranscriptPath(state, record.AgentID); fallback != "" && fallback != record.DeclaredTranscriptPath {
   381				candidates = append(candidates, fallback)
   382			}
   383			if len(candidates) == 0 {
   384				payload.TranscriptUnavailableReason = taskTranscriptReasonUnresolvable
   385				payloads = append(payloads, payload)
   386				continue
   387			}
   388	
   389			// A transcript is about to be read and, if valid, stored as
   390			// agent-<agent-id>.jsonl — the agent ID becomes part of that path, so
   391			// it must be present and path-safe before going any further. Skip the
   392			// WHOLE record rather than merely omitting the transcript: this is
   393			// the same "poisoned identifier" shape as the ToolUseID check above.
   394			if record.AgentID == "" || validation.ValidateAgentID(record.AgentID) != nil {
   395				logging.Warn(logCtx, "skipping task record: unsafe or missing agent_id",
   396					slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   397					slog.String("tool_use_id", record.ToolUseID),
   398				)
   399				continue
   400			}
   401	
   402			raw, transcriptPath, readErr := readFirstTranscript(candidates)
   403			if readErr != nil {
   404				logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to read subagent transcript; storing task without it",
   405					slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   406					slog.String("tool_use_id", record.ToolUseID),
   407					slog.String("error", readErr.Error()),
   408				)
   409				payload.TranscriptUnavailableReason = taskTranscriptReasonUnreadable
   410				payloads = append(payloads, payload)
   411				continue
   412			}
   413			if len(raw) == 0 {
   414				payload.TranscriptUnavailableReason = taskTranscriptReasonEmpty
   415				payloads = append(payloads, payload)
   416				continue
   417			}
   418	
   419			redacted, taskAssets, tooLarge, prepErr := prepareTaskTranscriptForStorage(ctx, logCtx, ag, state, transcriptPath, raw)
   420			if tooLarge {
   421				payload.TranscriptUnavailableReason = taskTranscriptReasonTooLarge
   422				payloads = append(payloads, payload)
   423				continue
   424			}
   425			if prepErr != nil {
   426				logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to redact subagent transcript; storing task without it",
   427					slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   428					slog.String("tool_use_id", record.ToolUseID),
   429					slog.String("error", prepErr.Error()),
   430				)
   431				payload.TranscriptUnavailableReason = taskTranscriptReasonRedactionFailed
   432				payloads = append(payloads, payload)
   433				continue
   434			}
   435	
   436			payload.Transcript = redacted
   437			assets = append(assets, taskAssets...)
   438			payloads = append(payloads, payload)
   439		}
   440	
   441		return payloads, assets
   442	}
   443	
   444	// readFirstTranscript tries each candidate path in order and returns the bytes
   445	// of the first one that reads successfully, along with the path it came from
   446	// (for logging — never for storage). Returns the last error when every
   447	// candidate fails (callers only reach here with at least one candidate).
   448	func readFirstTranscript(candidates []string) ([]byte, string, error) {
   449		var lastErr error
   450		for _, path := range candidates {
   451			data, err := os.ReadFile(path) //nolint:gosec // path is agent-declared or resolved from session state, not user input
   452			if err == nil {
   453				return data, path, nil
   454			}
   455			lastErr = err
   456		}
   457		return nil, "", lastErr
   458	}

   460	// sidecarSessionImages captures images an agent stores OUTSIDE the transcript
   461	// (e.g. Cursor's per-session SQLite blob store) as checkpoint assets, so they are
   462	// preserved with the session even though they never appear in full.jsonl. Unlike
   463	// externalizeSessionImages there is no transcript placeholder and no round trip:
   464	// these assets are preserve/view-only (the agent reads its own store on restore).
   465	//
   466	// Gated on the same opt-in flag. Best-effort: agents without the capability, or
   467	// any capture error, yield no assets (the checkpoint is written without them).
   468	func sidecarSessionImages(ctx, logCtx context.Context, ag agent.Agent, state *SessionState) []cpkg.TranscriptAsset {
   469		if !settings.IsImageExternalizationEnabled(ctx) {
   470			return nil
   471		}
   472		provider, ok := agent.AsSidecarImageProvider(ag)
   473		if !ok {
   474			return nil
   475		}
   476		assets, err := provider.SidecarImages(ctx, state.TranscriptPath)
   477		if err != nil {
   478			logging.Warn(logCtx, "sidecar image capture failed; checkpoint stored without them",
   479				slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   480				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   481			return nil
   482		}
   483		if len(assets) == 0 {
   484			return nil
   485		}
   486		out := make([]cpkg.TranscriptAsset, len(assets))
   487		for i, a := range assets {
   488			out[i] = cpkg.TranscriptAsset{Name: a.Name, MediaType: a.MediaType, Data: a.Data}
   489		}
   490		return out
   491	}

   493	// checkpointStepCount returns the number of user prompts attributed to the
   494	// checkpoint being written: the turns counted since the current window's base.
   495	// The base is re-anchored (deferred) the next time a turn is counted after a
   496	// checkpoint write, so back-to-back checkpoints with no prompt between them share
   497	// a count. Floored at 1 so we never record 0 (covers a fast-path checkpoint
   498	// before any turn, and exec-mode gaps where turns weren't counted). Attach has
   499	// its own count (see attachStepCount); it does not go through this path.
   500	func checkpointStepCount(s *SessionState) int {
   501		if w := s.SessionTurnCount - s.PromptWindowBase; w >= 1 {
   502			return w
   503		}
   504		return 1
   505	}

   507	// CondenseSession condenses a session's shadow branch to permanent storage.
   508	// checkpointID is the 12-hex-char value from the Entire-Checkpoint trailer.
   509	// Metadata is stored at sharded path: <checkpoint_id[:2]>/<checkpoint_id[2:]>/
   510	// Uses checkpoint.PersistentStore.Write with a checkpoint.Session request for persistent storage.
   511	//
   512	// For mid-session commits (no Stop/SaveStep called yet), the shadow branch may not exist.
   513	// In this case, data is extracted from the live transcript instead.
   514	func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) CondenseSession(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, state *SessionState, committedFiles map[string]struct{}, opts ...condenseOpts) (*CondenseResult, error) {
   515		ag, _ := agent.GetByAgentType(state.AgentType) //nolint:errcheck // ag may be nil for unknown agent types; callers use type assertions so nil is safe
   516		var o condenseOpts
   517		if len(opts) > 0 {
   518			o = opts[0]
   519		}
   520		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "checkpoint")
   521		condenseStart := time.Now()
   522		policy, err := readLocalCheckpointPolicy(logCtx, repo)
   523		if err != nil {
   524			return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoint policy could not be read: %w", err)
   525		}
   526		if !checkpointpolicy.CanSatisfyPolicy(policy) {
   527			warnIfCheckpointPolicyNeedsUpgrade(logCtx, policy)
   528			return nil, errors.New("checkpoint policy cannot be satisfied by this Entire CLI")
   529		}
   530	
   531		shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
   532		ref, hasShadowBranch := resolveShadowRef(repo, shadowBranchName, o.shadowRef)
   533	
   534		// Re-resolve transcript path before any reads — handles agents that relocate

   220	) (externalized []byte, assets []cpkg.TranscriptAsset, sanitizedSize int64) {
   221		sanitized := agent.SanitizeTranscriptForStorage(ag, raw)
   222		externalized, assets = externalizeSessionImages(ctx, logCtx, state, sanitized)
   223		return externalized, assets, int64(len(sanitized))
   224	}

   226	// prepareTaskTranscriptForStorage runs the sanitize -> externalize -> redact
   227	// chain for a single subagent transcript, mirroring prepareTranscriptForStorage's
   228	// first two steps and then completing with the same redaction the session
   229	// transcript gets (see redactSessionTranscript). It is a SEPARATE entry point
   230	// rather than a wrapper around prepareTranscriptForStorage for one reason:
   231	// that function returns the session transcript's sanitized SIZE, which seeds
   232	// CondenseResult.TranscriptSizeBaseline — the session's own growth-dedup
   233	// baseline (SessionState.CheckpointTranscriptSize). A task transcript must
   234	// NEVER contribute to that coordinate (it is not the session transcript), so
   235	// this helper only returns the pipeline's terminal artifacts: redacted bytes
   236	// and any externalized image assets. Callers append the assets to the
   237	// checkpoint's own Assets list (TaskPayload has no Assets field of its own).
   238	//
   239	// It also carries checkpoint.prepareSubagentTranscript's size guard, for the
   240	// same reason: agent-<agent-id>.jsonl is neither chunked nor capped, and
   240	// same reason: agent-<agent-id>.jsonl is neither chunked nor capped, and
   241	// redaction runs at roughly 220ms/MB. The cap is measured against the SANITIZED
   242	// bytes, not the raw ones — sanitizing strips the bulk (Codex encrypted_content
   243	// runs to ~20% of a rollout's bytes), so measuring raw would drop a transcript
   244	// oversized only by payloads about to be discarded.
   245	func prepareTaskTranscriptForStorage(
   246		ctx, logCtx context.Context,
   247		ag agent.Agent,
   248		state *SessionState,
   249		path string,
   250		raw []byte,
   251	) (redacted redact.RedactedBytes, assets []cpkg.TranscriptAsset, tooLarge bool, err error) {
   252		sanitized := agent.SanitizeTranscriptForStorage(ag, raw)
   253		if len(sanitized) > agent.MaxChunkSize {
   254			logging.Warn(logCtx, "subagent transcript exceeds the blob size cap; storing task without it",
   255				slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   256				slog.String("path", path),
   257				slog.Int("raw_bytes", len(raw)),
   258				slog.Int("sanitized_bytes", len(sanitized)),
   259				slog.Int("cap", agent.MaxChunkSize))
   260			return redact.RedactedBytes{}, nil, true, nil
   261		}
   262		externalized, assets := externalizeSessionImages(ctx, logCtx, state, sanitized)
   263		// nil repo declines prefix reuse: a subagent transcript is written once per
   264		// task, not appended across checkpoints, so there is nothing to reuse.
   265		redacted, _, err = redactSessionTranscript(logCtx, nil, "", externalized)
   266		if err != nil {
   267			return redact.RedactedBytes{}, nil, false, err
   268		}
   269		return redacted, assets, false, nil
   270	}

   272	// resolveTaskTranscriptPath falls back to the agent-layout convention when a
   273	// task record has no declared transcript path (e.g. an agent that reports the
   274	// path only on some events, or a legacy record captured before an agent
   275	// started reporting one at all). Mirrors cli.ResolveAgentTranscriptPath,
   276	// which this package cannot call directly — the cli package imports strategy,
   277	// so the reverse import would cycle — and the logic itself is small enough
   278	// that duplicating it here beats introducing a new shared package for this
   279	// one call site (moving the transcript resolver into paths is deliberately
   280	// out of scope for the durable-records plan this implements).
   281	func resolveTaskTranscriptPath(state *SessionState, agentID string) string {
   282		if agentID == "" || state.TranscriptPath == "" {
   283			return ""
   284		}
   285		transcriptDir := filepath.Dir(state.TranscriptPath)
   286		name := paths.AgentTranscriptFileName(agentID)
   287		if nested := filepath.Join(paths.SubagentsDir(transcriptDir, state.SessionID), name); fileExists(nested) {
   288			return nested
   289		}
   290		if legacy := filepath.Join(transcriptDir, name); fileExists(legacy) {
   291			return legacy
   292		}
   293		return ""
   294	}
   295	
   296	// taskTranscriptReasonUnresolvable, taskTranscriptReasonUnreadable,
   297	// taskTranscriptReasonEmpty, taskTranscriptReasonRedactionFailed, and
   298	// taskTranscriptReasonTooLarge are the stable
   299	// TaskPayload.TranscriptUnavailableReason categories. They deliberately
   300	// carry no path or underlying-error detail: task.json is pushed to
   301	// entire/checkpoints/v1, so a local filesystem path (which os.ReadFile's error
   302	// text embeds) must never end up in it. The detailed error goes only to
   303	// logging.Warn at the call site.
   304	const (
   305		taskTranscriptReasonUnresolvable    = "transcript path unresolvable"
   306		taskTranscriptReasonUnreadable      = "transcript unreadable"
   307		taskTranscriptReasonEmpty           = "transcript empty"
   308		taskTranscriptReasonRedactionFailed = "transcript redaction failed"
   309		taskTranscriptReasonTooLarge        = "transcript too large"
   310	)
   311	
   312	// materializeTaskRecords resolves and redacts each of state.TaskRecords'
   313	// subagent transcripts for storage under this checkpoint's
   314	// tasks/<tool-use-id>/ subtree — the durable-records materializer for #2058:
   315	// subagent transcripts used to die at condensation because no producer ever
   316	// set the (now deleted) WriteOptions.IsTask route.
   317	//
   318	// Every record is materialized on every condensation, whether completed or
   319	// still in flight: a completed record's transcript is stored once here and
   320	// then removed from session state by the caller (see resetCheckpointWindow);
   321	// an in-flight record's transcript-so-far is stored and the record stays so
   322	// the next condensation re-materializes it. A record whose transcript cannot
   323	// be resolved or read still produces a payload — with TranscriptUnavailableReason
   324	// set instead of a Transcript — so the pointer is never silently dropped.
   325	//
   326	// A record with an unsafe or empty ToolUseID, or one whose AgentID is unsafe
   327	// or empty at the point a transcript would be written, is skipped entirely —
   328	// no payload at all, not even a reason-only one: an unsafe ToolUseID has no
   329	// safe tasks/<id>/ directory to put a task.json under in the first place, and
   330	// an empty/unsafe AgentID would corrupt the agent-<id>.jsonl filename (see
   331	// writeTaskRecordEntries, which re-validates as a last resort). This must
   332	// never wedge condensation — a poisoned record produces zero payloads, not an
   333	// error, and the caller's normal completed-record removal
   334	// (resetCheckpointWindow) still drops it once completed, since a record that
   335	// can never materialize would otherwise retry forever.
   336	//
   337	// Task assets are appended to the incoming assets slice and returned (rather
   338	// than living on TaskPayload, which has no Assets field of its own) so they
   339	// join the checkpoint's own Assets list — see WriteOptions.Assets.
   340	func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) materializeTaskRecords(
   341		ctx, logCtx context.Context,
   342		ag agent.Agent,
   343		state *SessionState,
   344		assets []cpkg.TranscriptAsset,
   345	) ([]cpkg.TaskPayload, []cpkg.TranscriptAsset) {
   346		if len(state.TaskRecords) == 0 {
   347			return nil, assets
   348		}
   349	
   350		payloads := make([]cpkg.TaskPayload, 0, len(state.TaskRecords))
   351		for _, record := range state.TaskRecords {
   352			if record.ToolUseID == "" || validation.ValidateToolUseID(record.ToolUseID) != nil {
   353				logging.Warn(logCtx, "skipping task record: unsafe or empty tool_use_id",
   354					slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   355					slog.String("tool_use_id", record.ToolUseID),
   356				)
   357				continue
   358			}
   359	
   360			payload := cpkg.TaskPayload{
   361				ToolUseID:       record.ToolUseID,
   362				AgentID:         record.AgentID,
   363				SubagentType:    record.SubagentType,
   364				TaskDescription: record.TaskDescription,
   365				Files:           record.Files,
   366				TokenUsage:      record.TokenUsage,
   367				StartedAt:       record.StartedAt,
   368				CompletedAt:     record.CompletedAt,
   369			}
   370	
   371			// Candidate transcript paths, tried in order: the agent-declared path
   372			// first, then the agent-layout fallback — declared paths are
   373			// unreliable (agents relocate/clean up transcripts), which is why the
   374			// fallback resolver exists at all, so a declared-but-unreadable path
   375			// must not short-circuit past it.
   376			var candidates []string
   377			if record.DeclaredTranscriptPath != "" {
   378				candidates = append(candidates, record.DeclaredTranscriptPath)
   379			}
   380			if fallback := resolveTaskTranscriptPath(state, record.AgentID); fallback != "" && fallback != record.DeclaredTranscriptPath {
   381				candidates = append(candidates, fallback)
   382			}
   383			if len(candidates) == 0 {
   384				payload.TranscriptUnavailableReason = taskTranscriptReasonUnresolvable
   385				payloads = append(payloads, payload)
   386				continue
   387			}
   388	
   389			// A transcript is about to be read and, if valid, stored as
   390			// agent-<agent-id>.jsonl — the agent ID becomes part of that path, so
   391			// it must be present and path-safe before going any further. Skip the
   392			// WHOLE record rather than merely omitting the transcript: this is
   393			// the same "poisoned identifier" shape as the ToolUseID check above.
   394			if record.AgentID == "" || validation.ValidateAgentID(record.AgentID) != nil {
   395				logging.Warn(logCtx, "skipping task record: unsafe or missing agent_id",
   396					slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   397					slog.String("tool_use_id", record.ToolUseID),
   398				)
   399				continue
   400			}
   401	
   402			raw, transcriptPath, readErr := readFirstTranscript(candidates)
   403			if readErr != nil {
   404				logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to read subagent transcript; storing task without it",
   405					slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   406					slog.String("tool_use_id", record.ToolUseID),
   407					slog.String("error", readErr.Error()),
   408				)
   409				payload.TranscriptUnavailableReason = taskTranscriptReasonUnreadable
   410				payloads = append(payloads, payload)
   411				continue
   412			}
   413			if len(raw) == 0 {
   414				payload.TranscriptUnavailableReason = taskTranscriptReasonEmpty
   415				payloads = append(payloads, payload)
   416				continue
   417			}
   418	
   419			redacted, taskAssets, tooLarge, prepErr := prepareTaskTranscriptForStorage(ctx, logCtx, ag, state, transcriptPath, raw)
   420			if tooLarge {
   421				payload.TranscriptUnavailableReason = taskTranscriptReasonTooLarge
   422				payloads = append(payloads, payload)
   423				continue
   424			}
   425			if prepErr != nil {
   426				logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to redact subagent transcript; storing task without it",
   427					slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   428					slog.String("tool_use_id", record.ToolUseID),
   429					slog.String("error", prepErr.Error()),
   430				)
   431				payload.TranscriptUnavailableReason = taskTranscriptReasonRedactionFailed
   432				payloads = append(payloads, payload)
   433				continue
   434			}
   435	
   436			payload.Transcript = redacted
   437			assets = append(assets, taskAssets...)
   438			payloads = append(payloads, payload)
   439		}
   440	
   441		return payloads, assets
   442	}
   443	
   444	// readFirstTranscript tries each candidate path in order and returns the bytes
   445	// of the first one that reads successfully, along with the path it came from
   446	// (for logging — never for storage). Returns the last error when every
   447	// candidate fails (callers only reach here with at least one candidate).
   448	func readFirstTranscript(candidates []string) ([]byte, string, error) {
   449		var lastErr error
   450		for _, path := range candidates {
   451			data, err := os.ReadFile(path) //nolint:gosec // path is agent-declared or resolved from session state, not user input
   452			if err == nil {
   453				return data, path, nil
   454			}
   455			lastErr = err
   456		}
   457		return nil, "", lastErr
   458	}

   460	// sidecarSessionImages captures images an agent stores OUTSIDE the transcript
   461	// (e.g. Cursor's per-session SQLite blob store) as checkpoint assets, so they are
   462	// preserved with the session even though they never appear in full.jsonl. Unlike
   463	// externalizeSessionImages there is no transcript placeholder and no round trip:
   464	// these assets are preserve/view-only (the agent reads its own store on restore).
   465	//
   466	// Gated on the same opt-in flag. Best-effort: agents without the capability, or
   467	// any capture error, yield no assets (the checkpoint is written without them).
   468	func sidecarSessionImages(ctx, logCtx context.Context, ag agent.Agent, state *SessionState) []cpkg.TranscriptAsset {
   469		if !settings.IsImageExternalizationEnabled(ctx) {
   470			return nil
   471		}
   472		provider, ok := agent.AsSidecarImageProvider(ag)
   473		if !ok {
   474			return nil
   475		}
   476		assets, err := provider.SidecarImages(ctx, state.TranscriptPath)
   477		if err != nil {
   478			logging.Warn(logCtx, "sidecar image capture failed; checkpoint stored without them",
   479				slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   480				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   481			return nil
   482		}
   483		if len(assets) == 0 {
   484			return nil
   485		}
   486		out := make([]cpkg.TranscriptAsset, len(assets))
   487		for i, a := range assets {
   488			out[i] = cpkg.TranscriptAsset{Name: a.Name, MediaType: a.MediaType, Data: a.Data}
   489		}
   490		return out
   491	}
   492	
   493	// checkpointStepCount returns the number of user prompts attributed to the
   494	// checkpoint being written: the turns counted since the current window's base.
   495	// The base is re-anchored (deferred) the next time a turn is counted after a
   496	// checkpoint write, so back-to-back checkpoints with no prompt between them share
   497	// a count. Floored at 1 so we never record 0 (covers a fast-path checkpoint
   498	// before any turn, and exec-mode gaps where turns weren't counted). Attach has
   499	// its own count (see attachStepCount); it does not go through this path.
   500	func checkpointStepCount(s *SessionState) int {
   501		if w := s.SessionTurnCount - s.PromptWindowBase; w >= 1 {
   502			return w
   503		}
   504		return 1
   505	}

   507	// CondenseSession condenses a session's shadow branch to permanent storage.
   508	// checkpointID is the 12-hex-char value from the Entire-Checkpoint trailer.
   509	// Metadata is stored at sharded path: <checkpoint_id[:2]>/<checkpoint_id[2:]>/
   510	// Uses checkpoint.PersistentStore.Write with a checkpoint.Session request for persistent storage.
   511	//
   512	// For mid-session commits (no Stop/SaveStep called yet), the shadow branch may not exist.
   513	// In this case, data is extracted from the live transcript instead.
   514	func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) CondenseSession(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, state *SessionState, committedFiles map[string]struct{}, opts ...condenseOpts) (*CondenseResult, error) {
   515		ag, _ := agent.GetByAgentType(state.AgentType) //nolint:errcheck // ag may be nil for unknown agent types; callers use type assertions so nil is safe
   516		var o condenseOpts
   517		if len(opts) > 0 {
   518			o = opts[0]
   519		}
   520		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "checkpoint")
   521		condenseStart := time.Now()
   522		policy, err := readLocalCheckpointPolicy(logCtx, repo)
   523		if err != nil {
   524			return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoint policy could not be read: %w", err)
   525		}
   526		if !checkpointpolicy.CanSatisfyPolicy(policy) {
   527			warnIfCheckpointPolicyNeedsUpgrade(logCtx, policy)
   528			return nil, errors.New("checkpoint policy cannot be satisfied by this Entire CLI")
   529		}
   530	
   531		shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
   532		ref, hasShadowBranch := resolveShadowRef(repo, shadowBranchName, o.shadowRef)
   533	
   534		// Re-resolve transcript path before any reads — handles agents that relocate
   535		// transcripts mid-session (e.g., Cursor CLI flat → nested layout change).
   536		// Errors are ignored; downstream readers handle missing transcripts gracefully.
   537		resolveTranscriptPath(state) //nolint:errcheck,gosec // best-effort; downstream readers handle missing files
   538	
   539		extractStart := time.Now()
   540		_, extractSessionDataSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "extract_session_data")
   540		_, extractSessionDataSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "extract_session_data")
   541		var shadowHash plumbing.Hash
   542		if hasShadowBranch {
   543			shadowHash = ref.Hash()
   544		}
   545		sessionData, extractErr := s.extractOrCreateSessionData(ctx, repo, ag, shadowHash, hasShadowBranch, state)
   546		if extractErr != nil {
   547			extractSessionDataSpan.RecordError(extractErr)
   548			extractSessionDataSpan.End()
   549			return nil, extractErr
   550		}
   551		extractSessionDataSpan.End()
   552		extractDuration := time.Since(extractStart)
   553	
   554		// Backfill session state token usage from the freshly-extracted transcript.
   555		// Copilot CLI writes session.shutdown after the hooks return, so by condensation
   556		// time we can recover the authoritative full-session total from the transcript
   557		// while keeping checkpoint metadata scoped to CheckpointTranscriptStart. The
   558		// recompute drops SubagentTokens (subagentsDir=""); the helper preserves the
   559		// cumulative subagent total across the backfill so resetCheckpointWindow's
   560		// baseline does not regress to nil (finding 019f5ebf-a57e).
   561		applyBackfilledSessionTokenUsage(ctx, ag, state, sessionData.Transcript, sessionData.TokenUsage)
   562	
   563		if !hasTokenUsageData(sessionData.TokenUsage) && hasTokenUsageData(state.CheckpointTokenUsage) {
   564			// Whole-value fallback: accumulateTokenUsage already carries SubagentTokens.
   565			sessionData.TokenUsage = accumulateTokenUsage(nil, state.CheckpointTokenUsage)
   566		} else {
   567			// Refill only the subagent total the recompute dropped. Runs after
   568			// applyBackfilledSessionTokenUsage, which needs the usage without it.
   569			sessionData.TokenUsage = withSubagentTokensFrom(sessionData.TokenUsage, state.CheckpointTokenUsage)
   570		}
   571	
   572		// Backfill the model from the transcript for agents that don't report it via
   573		// hooks (e.g., Pi records message.model but its hook events carry no model
   574		// field). Only fills when the model is otherwise unknown — hook-reported
   575		// models take precedence.
   576		if state.ModelName == "" {
   577			if model := sessionStateBackfillModel(ctx, ag, sessionData.Transcript); model != "" {
   578				state.ModelName = model
   579			}
   580		}
   581	
   582		if skipped := skipIfNothingToCondense(logCtx, sessionData, state, checkpointID, hasShadowBranch); skipped != nil {
   583			return skipped, nil
   584		}
   585	
   586		filterFilesTouched(sessionData, committedFiles, state)
   587	
   588		// sessionData.Transcript is left as the raw transcript; only the sanitized,
   589		// externalized, redacted copy is stored.
   590		externalizedTranscript, extractedAssets, transcriptSizeBaseline := prepareTranscriptForStorage(ctx, logCtx, ag, state, sessionData.Transcript)
   591	
   592		redactedTranscript, redactDuration := redactOrDrop(logCtx, repo, state.SessionID, externalizedTranscript, checkpointID)
   593		if skipped := skipIfPostRedactionEmpty(logCtx, redactedTranscript, sessionData, state, checkpointID); skipped != nil {
   594			return skipped, nil
   595		}
   596	
   597		// Telemetry-only search probe, computed exactly once for every result this
   598		// function can return (the recovery result below included) so no
   599		// construction site can ship the zero value by omission — the fabricated
   600		// negative searchProbe.measured exists to catch. Gated: the scan is a
   601		// full-transcript pass, and only the PostCommit path, with telemetry
   602		// enabled, has a reader for it. detectSearchUsage maps a nil agent or
   603		// empty transcript to unsupported, which is the honest answer for the
   604		// no-transcript extraction branch.
   605		if o.searchProbeAllowed != nil && o.searchProbeAllowed() {
   606			sessionData.SearchProbe = detectSearchUsage(ag, sessionData.Transcript)
   607		}
   608	
   609		// Capture agent sidecar images (e.g. Cursor's SQLite store) after the skip
   610		// check, so the sqlite3 shell-out is avoided when the checkpoint is discarded.
   611		extractedAssets = append(extractedAssets, sidecarSessionImages(ctx, logCtx, ag, state)...)
   612	
   613		// Materialize this session's subagent task records (#2058): every
   614		// completed-or-in-flight record's transcript is resolved, redacted, and
   615		// stored under this checkpoint's tasks/<tool-use-id>/ subtree.
   616		taskPayloads, extractedAssets := s.materializeTaskRecords(ctx, logCtx, ag, state, extractedAssets)
   617	
   618		store, err := s.getPersistentStore(ctx, repo)
   619		if err != nil {
   620			return nil, err
   621		}
   622		recovery := recoverInterruptedCondensation(
   623			ctx, logCtx,
   624			o.reconcileInterrupted && state.NeedsCondensationRecovery(),
   625			store, state, redactedTranscript, extractedAssets, sessionData, transcriptSizeBaseline,
   626		)
   627		if recovery.done {
   628			return recovery.result, recovery.err
   629		}
   630	
   631		writeOpts, attributionDuration, newSkillEvents := buildCondensationWriteOptions(
   632			ctx, repo, ref, state, sessionData, redactedTranscript, extractedAssets,
   633			taskPayloads, checkpointID, shadowBranchName, o,
   634		)
   635	
   636		writeV1Start := time.Now()
   637		writeCtx, writeCommittedSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "write_committed_v1")
   638		writeRequest := condensationSessionWriteRequest(writeOpts)
   639		if err := store.Write(writeCtx, writeRequest); err != nil {
   640			writeCommittedSpan.RecordError(err)
   641			writeCommittedSpan.End()
   642			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to write checkpoint metadata: %w", err)
   643		}
   644		writeCommittedSpan.End()
   645		writeV1Duration := time.Since(writeV1Start)
   646	
   647		// Deferred prompt-window reset: a checkpoint was written, so the window base
   648		// must be re-anchored — but not now. We defer until the next counted turn (in
   649		// persistEventMetadataToState) so two checkpoints with no prompt between them
   650		// report the same count instead of the second showing 0.
   651		state.PromptWindowResetPending = true
   652	
   653		logging.Debug(logCtx, "condense timings",
   654			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   655			slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
   656			slog.Int64("extract_session_data_ms", extractDuration.Milliseconds()),
   657			slog.Int64("calculate_session_attribution_ms", attributionDuration.Milliseconds()),
   658			slog.Int64("redact_transcript_ms", redactDuration.Milliseconds()),
   659			slog.Int64("write_committed_v1_ms", writeV1Duration.Milliseconds()),
   660			slog.Int64("total_ms", time.Since(condenseStart).Milliseconds()),
   661			slog.Int("transcript_bytes", len(sessionData.Transcript)),
   662			slog.Int("transcript_lines", sessionData.FullTranscriptLines),
   663		)
   664	
   665		return &CondenseResult{
   666			CheckpointID:           checkpointID,
   667			SessionID:              state.SessionID,
   668			CheckpointsCount:       checkpointStepCount(state),
   669			FilesTouched:           sessionData.FilesTouched,
   670			Prompts:                sessionData.Prompts,
   671			TotalTranscriptLines:   sessionData.FullTranscriptLines,
   672			TranscriptSizeBaseline: transcriptSizeBaseline,
   673			NewSkillEvents:         newSkillEvents,
   674			SearchProbe:            sessionData.SearchProbe,
   675		}, nil
   676	}
   677	
   678	// condensationSessionWriteRequest returns the write request for one
   679	// condensation. Every condensation write is ReservedSession, unconditionally.
   680	//
   681	// The tempting refinement — send ReservedSession only when this session's own
   682	// pending attempt matches the checkpoint ID, and plain Session otherwise —
   683	// is wrong, and wrong in a worse direction than the problem it solves. A
   684	// checkpoint can hold several sessions, and only the one that reserved the ID
   685	// carries the reservation in its state. Routing per session would send the
   686	// reserving session's write to the backend the ID belongs to and every sibling's
   687	// write to the configured primary, splitting one checkpoint across both
   688	// backends. Reads are not symmetrical about that: a ULID resolves from git-refs
   689	// only, so the siblings written to the branch would simply be invisible. See
   690	// TestCondensationSessionWrites_KeepSharedReservedCheckpointInOneBackend.
   691	//

   678	// condensationSessionWriteRequest returns the write request for one
   679	// condensation. Every condensation write is ReservedSession, unconditionally.
   680	//
   681	// The tempting refinement — send ReservedSession only when this session's own
   682	// pending attempt matches the checkpoint ID, and plain Session otherwise —
   683	// is wrong, and wrong in a worse direction than the problem it solves. A
   684	// checkpoint can hold several sessions, and only the one that reserved the ID
   685	// carries the reservation in its state. Routing per session would send the
   686	// reserving session's write to the backend the ID belongs to and every sibling's
   687	// write to the configured primary, splitting one checkpoint across both
   688	// backends. Reads are not symmetrical about that: a ULID resolves from git-refs
   689	// only, so the siblings written to the branch would simply be invisible. See
   690	// TestCondensationSessionWrites_KeepSharedReservedCheckpointInOneBackend.
   691	//
   692	// The cost of routing everything by ID format is narrow. It only diverges from
   693	// the configured primary when the ID's format disagrees with the primary, and
   694	// the two fail-soft defaults agree: GenerateCheckpointID mints hex when the
   695	// checkpoints config cannot be read, and resolvePrimaryType defaults to
   696	// git-branch on the same unreadable config. Reaching a mismatch on a *fresh* ID
   697	// therefore takes a config read that succeeds for one call and fails for the
   698	// other — and even then the checkpoint stays readable, because a hex ID under a
   699	// git-refs primary falls through to the branch on read.
   700	//
   701	// If the per-checkpoint routing decision ever does need to be conditional, it
   702	// has to be made once for the whole checkpoint (from the commit trailer or a
   703	// checkpoint-level flag), never per session.
   704	func condensationSessionWriteRequest(opts cpkg.WriteOptions) cpkg.WriteRequest {
   705		return cpkg.ReservedSession(opts)
   706	}

   113		// PostCommit must NOT: its ID comes from the commit's Entire-Checkpoint
   114		// trailer, which is already written and cannot be revised. Redirecting the
   115		// write there leaves the commit naming a checkpoint that was never stored,
   116		// and updateCombinedAttributionForCheckpoint writing attribution under the
   117		// same non-existent ID.
   118		reconcileInterrupted bool

   120		// searchProbeAllowed gates the telemetry-only search-usage transcript scan
   121		// (detectSearchUsage). nil or false means don't scan: the probe then stays
   122		// its zero value, which the payload layer refuses to present as a
   123		// measurement (searchProbe.measured). Only PostCommit — the sole path that

   125		// session-end condensation paths never scan because nothing would read the
   126		// result. The gate is memoized per commit by commitCondensedEmitter, so the
   127		// settings load behind it runs at most once per PostCommit.
   128		searchProbeAllowed func() bool

   131	// redactSessionJSONLBytes runs the regex-only redaction pipeline (the
   132	// eight always-on/opt-in layers) over a session transcript at
   133	// post-commit condensation. OPF is intentionally NOT included here —
   134	// it runs exclusively in the pre-push rewrite path
   135	// (strategy/manual_commit_opf_rewrite.go), which re-redacts the
   136	// regex-only blobs and produces OPF-applied (9-layer) commits before
   137	// the push.
   138	//
   139	// Exposed as a var so tests can inject deterministic success/error
   140	// returns. The signature still takes a context so the var can be
   141	// re-wired to JSONLBytesWithPrivacyFilter from tests that need OPF.

   146	// extractSessionImages lifts inline base64 images out of a transcript into
   147	// externalized assets via the per-agent image codec, returning the rewritten
   148	// (placeholder-bearing) transcript. Agents with no codec, or transcripts with no
   149	// externalizable images, pass through unchanged. Injectable for tests.
   150	var extractSessionImages = func(agentType types.AgentType, transcript []byte) ([]byte, []cpkg.TranscriptAsset, error) {
   151		codec := imageextract.CodecFor(agentType)
   152		if codec == nil {
   153			return transcript, nil, nil
   154		}
   155		rewritten, assets, err := codec.ExtractImages(transcript)
   156		if err != nil {
   157			return transcript, nil, fmt.Errorf("extract images: %w", err)
   158		}
   159		if len(assets) == 0 {
   160			return transcript, nil, nil
   161		}
   162		out := make([]cpkg.TranscriptAsset, len(assets))
   163		for i, a := range assets {
   164			out[i] = cpkg.TranscriptAsset{Name: a.Name, MediaType: a.MediaType, Data: a.Data}
   165		}
   166		return rewritten, out, nil
   167	}

   169	// externalizeSessionImages runs the opt-in image-externalization step over a
   170	// session transcript before redaction. When enabled it returns the rewritten
   171	// (placeholder-bearing) transcript plus the extracted assets; when disabled,
   172	// unsupported for the agent, or on error it returns the transcript unchanged with
   173	// nil assets (the checkpoint then stores the inline transcript).
   174	//
   175	// It deliberately does NOT mutate the caller's transcript: the pre-externalization
   176	// bytes are what CondenseResult.TranscriptSizeBaseline is measured on, and that
   177	// baseline must stay in the shadow-branch blob's coordinate (sanitized but NOT
   178	// image-externalized, matching what the Stop path writes) — feeding it the shrunken
   179	// externalized size would report spurious growth on every subsequent commit.
   180	func externalizeSessionImages(ctx, logCtx context.Context, state *SessionState, transcript []byte) ([]byte, []cpkg.TranscriptAsset) {
   181		if !settings.IsImageExternalizationEnabled(ctx) {
   182			return transcript, nil
   183		}
   184		rewritten, assets, err := extractSessionImages(state.AgentType, transcript)
   185		if err != nil {
   186			logging.Warn(logCtx, "image externalization failed; leaving transcript inline",
   187				slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   188				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   189			return transcript, nil
   190		}
   191		return rewritten, assets
   192	}

   194	// prepareTranscriptForStorage runs the first two steps of the stored-copy pipeline
   195	// in order — sanitize (drop non-portable agent state), then externalize inline
   196	// images. Redaction is the caller's next step, so the whole pipeline reads
   197	// sanitize -> externalize -> redact. See prepareTaskTranscriptForStorage for
   198	// the twin that runs the same pipeline over a subagent's own transcript.
   199	//
   200	// Each step has to precede the next:
   201	//
   202	//   - Sanitize first, so we neither externalize images out of items we are about to
   203	//     discard — which would store an asset whose referencing transcript line is gone
   204	//     moments later — nor redact megabytes of ciphertext only to throw it away.
   205	//     Base64 is the pathological input for the entropy layer, so on a large Codex
   206	//     rollout that scan alone costs tens of seconds.
   207	//   - Externalize before redaction, because base64 is high-entropy and redaction
   208	//     would otherwise flag and destroy it.
   209	//
   210	// It returns the sanitized size rather than the sanitized bytes: that size is the
   211	// coordinate the CheckpointTranscriptSize growth baseline must use (see
   212	// CondenseResult.TranscriptSizeBaseline), and returning the slice would keep a
   213	// second multi-MB buffer reachable for the rest of the condensation just to read
   214	// its length.
   215	func prepareTranscriptForStorage(
   216		ctx, logCtx context.Context,
   217		ag agent.Agent,
   218		state *SessionState,
   219		raw []byte,
   220	) (externalized []byte, assets []cpkg.TranscriptAsset, sanitizedSize int64) {
   221		sanitized := agent.SanitizeTranscriptForStorage(ag, raw)
   222		externalized, assets = externalizeSessionImages(ctx, logCtx, state, sanitized)
   223		return externalized, assets, int64(len(sanitized))
   224	}
